title: Why delayed dental care is rarely about not caring
summary: When a patient arrives with advanced dental disease, it is easy to focus on the visible damage: untreated decay, infection, pain, or tooth loss. The question often becomes, “Why did they wait so...
full_content:
When a patient arrives with advanced dental disease, it is easy to focus on the visible damage: untreated decay, infection, pain, or tooth loss. The question often becomes, “Why did they wait so long?” But that question can oversimplify a much more complicated reality. Delayed dental care is not always the result of indifference or poor personal choices. For many people, it reflects a combination of financial pressure, limited access, fear, language barriers, and uncertainty about when dental symptoms require professional attention.

The cost of waiting

For patients without dental insurance or with limited coverage, even a routine visit can feel financially risky. Many postpone care while trying to manage discomfort at home, hoping the problem will resolve on its own or remain tolerable until they can afford treatment. By the time pain becomes impossible to ignore, a condition that might have required a simple restoration may instead require root canal treatment, extraction, or emergency care. The delay is often interpreted as neglect, even though the patient may have been making a difficult financial decision between dental treatment and other essential expenses.

Fear can become a barrier to care

Dental anxiety is another major reason patients postpone treatment. Some have experienced pain, felt judged, or felt a loss of control during previous appointments. Others fear injections, drilling, bad news, or the cost of an unfamiliar procedure. Avoidance may provide temporary emotional relief, but it often allows disease to progress and makes the eventual visit more complex. When clinicians respond with criticism, they may reinforce the very fear that kept the patient away. A calm, nonjudgmental approach can help rebuild trust and make continued care more likely.

Language barriers and unclear information

Patients may also delay care because they do not fully understand what their symptoms mean or how urgently they should respond. Instructions filled with technical language can make it difficult to recognize early warning signs, compare treatment options, or understand the consequences of waiting. For patients with limited English proficiency, these challenges may become even greater when translated materials or qualified interpreters are unavailable. Clear, culturally responsive communication can help patients make informed decisions before a manageable problem becomes an emergency.

Access is more than having a dental office nearby

Transportation, inflexible work schedules, caregiving responsibilities, and long appointment wait times can make dental care difficult to obtain. Some patients cannot take unpaid time off or attend multiple visits without risking their income or employment. Others live in communities where few providers accept Medicaid or offer affordable treatment. A dental office may exist within driving distance, but that does not mean care is realistically accessible. When these practical barriers accumulate, postponing treatment may feel like the only available option.

The hidden role of oral health literacy

Even when dental services are available, patients may not know when to seek care or how to navigate the system. Early dental disease can progress without severe pain, leading some people to assume that treatment can wait. Others may not understand why preventive visits matter when nothing appears to be wrong. Oral health education should do more than tell people to brush and floss. It should help them recognize warning signs, understand the consequences of delay, and identify where to seek appropriate care.

What clinicians can do differently

Clinicians cannot remove every financial or structural barrier, but they can change how patients experience care. Instead of asking, “Why did you wait so long?” they can ask, “What made it difficult for you to come in sooner?” This small shift replaces blame with curiosity and may reveal concerns about cost, fear, transportation, language, or previous negative experiences. Clear explanations, realistic treatment priorities, and respectful discussion of affordable options can help patients regain a sense of control and remain engaged in care.

From judgment to understanding

Delayed dental care should not automatically be treated as evidence of irresponsibility. It often reflects the interaction of financial hardship, fear, limited access, competing responsibilities, and insufficient health information. Recognizing these barriers does not minimize the importance of personal responsibility. It allows clinicians to address the real reasons patients struggle to seek care.

When dental professionals replace judgment with empathy, clear communication, and practical support, they create a better opportunity for patients to return, complete treatment, and seek help earlier in the future. Instead of asking why a patient failed to come sooner, we should ask what clinicians and the health care system can do to make timely dental care more understandable, accessible, and achievable.

Daria Buinevich is a dentist, public health educator, and the founder and executive director of the CareGuard Initiative, an educational organization dedicated to improving oral health literacy through evidence-based resources and community outreach.

Her work focuses on translating scientific and public health recommendations into practical educational materials that help individuals and communities prevent oral diseases and make informed health decisions. She develops multilingual educational content, promotes preventive care, and advocates for accessible oral health education. Through writing and public engagement, she aims to bridge the gap between scientific evidence and everyday health practices while supporting healthier communities through education.

She has contributed to KevinMD, and shares her work on Substack, Medium, and LinkedIn.

title: A broken health care system and the physician shortage
summary: An excerpt from Failure to Treat: How a Broken Healthcare System Puts Patients and Providers at Risk. Over the course of my career, I have witnessed an inexorable decline in the quality of medical car...
full_content:
An excerpt from Failure to Treat: How a Broken Healthcare System Puts Patients and Providers at Risk.

Over the course of my career, I have witnessed an inexorable decline in the quality of medical care that we, as physicians, render to our patients. There is a myriad of reasons for this sad development, some the fault of physicians, but the majority caused by a health care system that is almost hopelessly broken.

I wrote Failure to Treat to inform the public about many of these ills. I used carefully anonymized true stories because I believe that narrative medicine is a powerful teaching tool, and because I developed a talent for storytelling during my tenure as a medical mystery author. I have been gratified by the reception my book has received. Virtually no one has disagreed with my posits. Everyone who reads the book is anxious to tell me about a medical misadventure that affected themselves or someone they love.

Despite success in educating the public and seeing some movement among our professional organizations, there continue to be developments that jeopardize the quality of care of all Americans. Passage of the Big Beautiful Bill put into motion massive cuts in social programs, most importantly medical insurance for the elderly and the disadvantaged. Insisting on proof of employment to retain Medicaid coverage will impose an impossible burden on patients and practitioners and will deprive millions of our most vulnerable citizens of medical coverage. Repealing tax subsidies for policies purchased on government exchanges has forced tens of millions to give up their insurance. We have recently learned that physicians who care for elderly patients in outpatient settings will be subjected to further cuts in their payments, reducing the number of medical trainees who will enter primary care specialties.

Prior authorization has made it possible for insurance companies to deny care to thousands of patients. Appealing these maddening decisions has contributed directly to physician burnout. Promised reform has not happened. In fact, CMS recently announced its intention to use artificial intelligence to make these critical decisions. Congressional efforts to block this misguided decision have failed.

The public is deluged with media advertisements for prescription drugs and medical devices. Not only does this practice raise the price of life-sustaining medications, but it has imposed yet another burden on experienced physicians who must explain why a drug on TV is inappropriate. Even worse, advertising for unproven or worthless remedies is rampant. Legislators have refused to close the loophole that allows “food derivatives” to be promoted for medicinal benefits they simply don’t possess. Administration officials contribute to the crisis with witless policy decisions. Witness the secretary of defense insisting on testosterone measurements for military personnel when there are no data to support claims of superior performance with supplementation.

Contrast this laissez-faire approach to snake oil products with the draconian approach regulators have taken with psychedelics. Despite strong evidence of efficacy for such poorly treated but common disorders as PTSD, the FDA has refused to approve any of these therapies. The thousands of veterans who suffer from PTSD should not be surprised by how lightly they are regarded. The VA hospital system has been victimized by funding cuts, causing massive personnel shortages.

Perhaps the most fundamental reason for the deterioration in the quality of care of Americans is physician undersupply. Not only are we not training enough primary care physicians, but we will be facing shortages of key specialists. Currently, over 40 percent of counties in the U.S. do not have a cardiologist, and shortfalls in that critical specialty will increase exponentially in the next ten years. Yet, our government has refused to take action, for example making it easier for well-educated foreign physicians to practice in the U.S.

At the back end, doctors are leaving the profession in droves. Physicians are retiring earlier or looking for things to do other than grinding through a 40-patient day in the office. They are spooked by the ever-increasing possibility of being sued while legislators refuse to rein in plaintiff lawyers who have drained billions from a struggling medical care system. They are tired of taking marching orders from bean counters who have no idea of what practice entails. They are done with having their free time eaten up by administrative tasks that justify payment but provide no improvement in patient care.

Physicians are also frustrated by their inability to keep up with the avalanche of new medical information. Medical science has moved quickly to develop a series of incredibly effective treatments for common diseases. Unfortunately, we have created a huge gap between what is happening at the scientific vanguard and what rank-and-file clinicians can implement. Given no time to read or attend conferences, physicians rely on top-line data on the internet. They practice cookbook medicine. “If you see this, then do that” medicine disadvantages patients who respond best to individualization of care.

Financiers in charge of medicine are driven by the bottom line, which means that controlling costs to maximize profits, especially in the world in which private equity rules, is paramount. Personnel costs are the low-hanging fruit. Restricting the number of nurses and paying them poorly is a common strategy that has resulted in nursing strikes across the country. When queried about why they are on a picket line, nurses answer that they fear for their patients more than they worry about their paycheck.

America spent over five trillion dollars on health care in 2025, or $16,000 per person. If the funds were spent wisely and equitably, we would be blessed with the best health care system in the world. Instead, we have allowed billions of dollars to be siphoned off by people who care only about their bank accounts and not about patients. We now have a health care system that ranks last in the world in almost every quality metric.

The situation is dire, but the solution is obvious. All of us, practitioners and patients, must pressure our legislators to enact laws to ensure that every single person in this country has access to the medical care they need and deserve.

Peter R. Kowey is professor of medicine and clinical pharmacology at Thomas Jefferson University, emeritus chief of the division of cardiovascular diseases at the Lankenau Heart Institute, and the William Wikoff Smith Chair in Cardiovascular Research at the Lankenau Institute for Medical Research.

Dr. Kowey is an internationally recognized expert in heart rhythm disorders. His research, regulatory, and clinical trial expertise have led to the development of innovative therapies for cardiac arrhythmias. He is the recipient of more than 150 grants, has written more than 450 papers and scientific reports, and has coedited five textbooks on cardiac arrhythmia. He has trained hundreds of fellows who practice cardiology and cardiac electrophysiology around the world.

Dr. Kowey is a fellow of the American Heart Association, the American College of Cardiology, the American College of Physicians, and the Heart Rhythm Society, along with several other professional organizations. He was a member of the Cardio-Renal Drug Advisory Committee and the Cardiovascular Devices Advisory Committee of the Food and Drug Administration. He has received numerous awards, including the Edward S. Cooper Award from the American Heart Association and the William Osler Award from the University of Miami.

Dr. Kowey is a graduate of St. Joseph’s University and the University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine. He completed his residency training in internal medicine at Penn State University and was a fellow in cardiovascular medicine and research at the Harvard University School of Public Health, the Peter Bent Brigham Hospital, and the West Roxbury VA Hospital. He has published six novels and is the author of the upcoming book Failure to Treat: How a Broken Healthcare System Puts Patients and Providers at Risk. He shares updates on Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, and Substack.

full_content:
普通用户最先感到的，不是模型参数变了，而是看病、说话、打游戏和找回账号都少了几步。ChatGPT Health把个人记录带进对话，也让错误建议的代价更具体。Amazon让Luna住进Prime Video，Google把自拍视频做成备用钥匙，Tesla门把手则被拉进安全规则。方便是真的。我的判断是：体验升级不能只算省了多少时间，还要把退出、撤销和求助做得同样顺手。

一起来看看这两天发生的AI和互联网赛道的大事件吧！

📌 今日AI互联网大事件速览

1，OpenAI向美国用户全面开放ChatGPT Health，健康记录与Apple Health可接入对话

2，ChatGPT健康建议引发近致命诉讼，AI医疗边界再受追问

3，Claude语音模式升级至Opus和Sonnet，邮件与协作场景可直接调用

4，Amazon升级Alexa Plus，复杂指令可跨品牌联动智能家居

5，AMD推出Helios机架级AI系统，微软等大客户计划规模部署

6，英伟达与Amkor签署15亿美元协议，美国先进封装产能继续扩张

7，微软将在经典版Outlook加入常驻Copilot入口，AI进一步嵌入邮件工作流

8，Google提出让大模型定期“睡觉”，用记忆巩固解决持续学习难题

9，马斯克呼吁全球AI实验室联合审查安全，愿与OpenAI放下分歧

10，腾讯Marvis聚焦系统级操作，上线两天日活突破30万

11，腾讯混元多模态负责人胡瀚离职创业，原团队或转向世界模型

12，阿里真武M890适配Qwen3.8，国产超节点跑通2.4万亿参数模型

13，阿里Accio Work用户达1000万，中小企业单次AI任务成本下降一半

14，阿里整合三款Agent产品，AI资源从多线探索转向集中投入

15，智谱建成1吉瓦国产芯片数据中心，模型公司开始自建算力底座

16，TikTok测试付费短剧应用LimeShorts，每周订阅价20美元

17，腾讯317万元年终奖截图泄露后续发酵，涉事员工被曝遭辞退

18，小米公布澎程增程器保养周期，首保后最长3年或3万公里

19，华为兆瓦超充获电网友好性认证，重卡补能开始兼顾电网压力

20，东风奕派M8正式上市，全系标配华为乾崑六件套

21，京东物流参与新会陈皮公共监管仓，地标农产品引入全程溯源

22，特斯拉隐藏式门把手推动美国酝酿新规，断电逃生成为监管重点

23，Meta退出RE100清洁能源倡议，AI数据中心天然气扩张引发质疑

24，Amazon把Luna云游戏接入Prime Video，会员可在电视端即点即玩

25，Google上线自拍视频登录备份，账号找回多了一把“人脸钥匙”

AI赛道观察

1. OpenAI向美国用户全面开放ChatGPT Health，健康记录与Apple Health可接入对话

核心内容：OpenAI开始向美国18岁以上的ChatGPT登录用户全面推出Health，覆盖Free、Go、Plus和Pro方案，并先在网页与iOS端开放。用户可自愿连接Apple Health及受支持的医疗记录，让模型结合检验结果、用药、睡眠、活动和既往就诊信息解释变化、整理就医问题。OpenAI称相关健康数据与对话采用额外加密，不用于训练基础模型或定向广告，产品定位是帮助用户理解信息而非替代医生。健康入口从通用问答走向个人记录后，便利明显提升，数据授权、误判提醒和紧急就医边界也会成为长期考验。

2. ChatGPT健康建议引发近致命诉讼，AI医疗边界再受追问

核心内容：美国佛罗里达州一名男子起诉OpenAI及CEO萨姆·奥尔特曼，称自己出现头晕和血压异常后多次咨询ChatGPT，却被建议无需立即就医，后来因双肺血栓导致肺栓塞，一度面临生命危险。案件目前只是原告指控，责任与事实仍待法院认定，但它与ChatGPT Health扩大开放形成鲜明反差：AI越深入个人健康场景，用户越容易把流畅回答当成专业判断。平台需要更明确识别高风险症状，优先建议线下急诊，并持续提醒模型不能完成诊断；用户也不能把聊天机器人当作医生替代品。

3. Claude语音模式升级至Opus和Sonnet，邮件与协作场景可直接调用

核心内容：Anthropic把Claude语音模式从速度更快的Haiku扩展至能力更强的Opus和Sonnet，用户在口头对话中也能调用更完整的推理与写作能力。获得授权后，语音模式还可读取Gmail、Google Calendar、Google Docs和Slack等连接应用的上下文，用于改约会议、整理邮件或起草回复。语音不再只是聊天界面的另一种输入方式，而是在用户走路、开会和处理事务时直接进入工作流。连接应用越多，Claude越有机会替用户完成连续任务，但误操作、敏感内容读取和每一步确认机制也必须同步加强。

4. Amazon升级Alexa Plus，复杂指令可跨品牌联动智能家居

核心内容：Amazon为预览阶段的Alexa Plus推出新一轮AI升级，使其能够理解更复杂的智能家居指令，并与Bosch、Delta、Ecovacs、iRobot等品牌设备建立新的联动方式。过去用户往往需要记住设备名称、房间和固定口令，新版本希望把这些规则压缩成更自然的表达，让助手自行拆解步骤。智能家居的竞争因此从“能不能联网”转向“能不能听懂并可靠执行”。真正影响普通家庭体验的仍是跨品牌兼容、断网可用、误触发后的撤销能力，以及摄像头、门锁等高敏感设备是否保留明确确认。

5. AMD推出Helios机架级AI系统，微软等大客户计划规模部署

核心内容：AMD在Advancing AI大会展示Helios机架级系统，准备于年内向客户出货，并把它定位为训练和运行大规模前沿模型的一体化基础设施。系统把GPU、EPYC处理器、网络与软件栈组织成完整机架，微软已计划在Azure规模部署，OpenAI、Meta、Oracle和Anthropic等也在客户名单中；Anthropic另计划通过Helios部署最高2吉瓦的AMD GPU。英伟达长期主导机架级市场，AMD此次不再只卖单颗芯片，而是争夺整套系统与集群标准。客户最终会看真实吞吐、能耗、软件迁移和长期供应，而不只看峰值参数。

6. 英伟达与Amkor签署15亿美元协议，美国先进封装产能继续扩张

核心内容：英伟达与美国本土大型封测企业Amkor达成多年战略合作，共同开发面向下一代AI与加速计算平台的先进封装和测试技术，协议价值约15亿美元。英伟达将提供预付款，支持Amkor扩建亚利桑那州产能，双方还将对齐高密度互连和异构集成的长期路线。Amkor当地先进封装园区总投资约70亿美元，预计2028年投产，并与台积电亚利桑那晶圆厂形成配套。AI芯片性能越来越依赖封装、内存和互连，产能本地化能增强供应韧性，但建设周期、成本和良率决定这笔投资能否真正缓解瓶颈。

7. 微软将在经典版Outlook加入常驻Copilot入口，AI进一步嵌入邮件工作流

核心内容：微软计划在8月为Windows 10和Windows 11上的经典版Outlook增加统一Copilot入口，并让按钮保持可见，把AI从独立应用进一步推到用户每天处理邮件和日程的界面。Copilot可用于概括长邮件、起草回复、整理会议信息和调用企业上下文，减少在不同窗口之间切换。常驻入口能提升发现率，却也容易让用户在不清楚数据范围时直接提交敏感内容。企业部署需要把许可证、邮箱权限、审计记录和人工复核一起配置好，尤其不能让“按钮随手可点”变成“内容默认可读”。

8. Google提出让大模型定期“睡觉”，用记忆巩固解决持续学习难题

核心内容：Google研究人员分享论文《Language Models Need Sleep》，尝试用类似“清醒—睡眠”的周期解决大模型持续学习问题。模型在清醒阶段接收新信息、执行任务，在睡眠阶段通过知识播种、广义蒸馏和强化学习生成的“梦境”数据整理记忆，把近期经验写入更稳定的能力，同时减少新知识覆盖旧知识。实验覆盖长程持续学习、知识吸收和少样本泛化，说明离线巩固阶段可能有价值。这仍是研究方案，并不等于模型已经具备人类式记忆；真正落地还要控制错误经验被反复强化、训练成本和用户数据边界。

9. 马斯克呼吁全球AI实验室联合审查安全，愿与OpenAI放下分歧

核心内容：埃隆·马斯克呼吁前沿AI实验室在新模型发布前共同审查安全问题，并向中美政府报告重大风险。他还称，为了全球利益，愿意放下与OpenAI CEO萨姆·奥尔特曼的个人与商业分歧展开合作。这个提议回应了模型能力评估碎片化的问题，但联合审查如何保持独立、哪些结果需要公开、政府怎样参与，都没有现成答案。实验室之间既是竞争对手又掌握关键测试数据，若缺少共同标准和外部监督，合作口号很难转化为可验证的安全机制。

10. 腾讯Marvis聚焦系统级操作，上线两天日活突破30万

核心内容：系统级Agent Marvis上线两天日活跃用户超过30万，七日留存约54%。与面向办公效率的WorkBuddy、继续运营但团队有所调整的QClaw不同，Marvis把重点放在操作系统层级的设备控制，不追求覆盖所有通用任务。腾讯希望利用应用宝的跨端能力，让Agent在电脑和设备上直接完成多步骤操作。快速起量说明用户对“替我点、替我做”有需求，但系统权限也比聊天框更敏感。产品后续要证明复杂任务成功率、端侧隐私模式和关键操作确认，而不只是靠入口导流。

11. 腾讯混元多模态负责人胡瀚离职创业，原团队或转向世界模型

核心内容：腾讯混元多模态理解负责人胡瀚被曝已提出离职并准备创业。胡瀚曾任微软亚洲研究院视觉计算组首席研究员，2025年初加入腾讯，随后进入大语言模型部的前沿研究组，负责多模态理解并参与世界模型研发。随着大语言模型部负责人姚顺雨梳理团队，胡瀚原研究组可能进一步聚焦世界模型与视觉推理。人员流动本身不代表路线成败，却反映多模态竞争正从识别图片和视频转向理解空间、因果与行动。腾讯能否保持研究连续性、把Hy3等模型接到真实产品，是这次调整更值得观察的部分。

12. 阿里真武M890适配Qwen3.8，国产超节点跑通2.4万亿参数模型

核心内容：阿里真武M890超节点完成对Qwen3.8的适配，并在阿里云百炼提供推理服务，被称为国内首个成功运行超2万亿参数大模型的超节点。Qwen3.8参数规模约2.4万亿，需要把模型分散到大量高速互联加速卡上，普通集群容易受通信带宽、延迟和并发限制。真武M890是平头哥新一代训推一体AI芯片，支持从FP32到FP4的多种精度。此次适配的意义不只是一项参数纪录，而是国产芯片、互连、编译和云平台能否组成可用系统；后续还需用吞吐、稳定性、成本和客户负载验证。

13. 阿里Accio Work用户达1000万，中小企业单次AI任务成本下降一半

核心内容：全球已有1000万中小企业使用跨境电商AI工作台Accio Work，一年内增长超过30倍。过去12个月，平台中小企业的Token消耗量增长10倍，而单次任务成本下降50%。Accio Work已接入阿里国际站、1688、淘宝、天猫和Shopify等平台，商家可围绕选品、营销和运营搭建AI团队，把多平台业务放进同一套工作流。规模增长和单位成本下降说明AI正在进入真实经营环节，但平台还要用成交、复购和节省的人力时间证明价值，避免Token增长只代表使用量而非经营结果。

14. 阿里整合三款Agent产品，AI资源从多线探索转向集中投入

核心内容：阿里近期整合QoderWork、悟空和MuleRun三款Agent产品，引发外界对内部“赛马”结束的讨论。更实际的变化是，大厂在经历一年多线探索后，开始重新判断哪些Agent能力值得继续投入，并把产品、模型、工程和入口资源向少数方向集中。三款产品原本面向不同任务，整合能减少重复建设，也可能让团队更快形成统一工作流和商业模式。风险在于过早收拢会牺牲差异化试验，过晚则持续消耗资源。最终判断标准不是组织架构，而是用户能否少配置一步、任务成功率是否提高、成本是否下降。

15. 智谱建成1吉瓦国产芯片数据中心，模型公司开始自建算力底座

核心内容：智谱被披露建成一座1吉瓦级AI数据中心，全部采用国产芯片，目前已开始部分运营并服务GLM模型与平台开发。相较只采购云端算力，模型公司自建数据中心可以更深地协同芯片、集群软件、训练框架和推理调度，也把电力、机房与利用率风险直接背到自己身上。全国产芯片集群若能在长期真实负载下稳定运行，将为受限环境中的大规模部署提供工程样本。不过1吉瓦代表巨大的建设与能耗规模，芯片可得并不等于系统高效，互连、故障恢复、软件兼容和Token成本仍需持续验证。

互联网赛道观察

16. TikTok测试付费短剧应用LimeShorts，每周订阅价20美元

核心内容：TikTok在美国测试付费短剧应用LimeShorts，产品今年3月开始小范围运行，采用免费内容加付费解锁模式。用户可按每周20美元或每年200美元订阅全部内容，也能购买虚拟金币按集付费；该应用已替代字节跳动此前的小说阅读产品Mytopia，并进入美国应用商店。TikTok还在推进免费短剧应用、主站内容流测试和原创剧合作，美国微短剧市场规模已约14亿美元。独立应用有利于建立付费习惯，但周订阅价格不低，内容更新速度、取消订阅是否清晰和单集质量会直接决定留存。

17. 腾讯317万元年终奖截图泄露后续发酵，涉事员工被曝遭辞退

核心内容：一张曾在社交平台广泛传播的腾讯员工收入截图，列出约82万元现金奖金和约235万元股票，年末激励总额约317万元。最新网络消息称，该员工因泄露薪酬信息被辞退、列入内部黑名单且不再录用。腾讯尚未对具体处理公开作出完整说明，因此相关细节仍应视为待核实信息。事件把大厂薪酬透明、员工保密义务和社交传播风险同时推到台前。无论最终处理如何，企业需要让保密边界与处分依据更清楚，员工也应意识到带有个人与公司信息的截图极易被追溯。

18. 小米公布澎程增程器保养周期，首保后最长3年或3万公里

核心内容：小米汽车公布澎程系列增程器维护方案，新车首次保养以整车1年或增程器运行1万公里为准，此后可延长至整车3年或增程器运行3万公里，以先到者为准。产品采用与东安动力深度定制的增程器和壳牌定制机油，小米称长周期来自大电池、纯电优先的使用方式及测试数据。更长保养间隔能减少车主到店次数和长期用车成本，但宣传周期仍要接受不同气候、工况与高频长途使用检验。厂商还需把保养触发条件、质保责任和车机提醒写得足够清楚，避免用户只记住“3年一次”。

19. 华为兆瓦超充获电网友好性认证，重卡补能开始兼顾电网压力

核心内容：华为数字能源的兆瓦超充方案获得电网友好性相关认证，显示超大功率充电不仅追求缩短补能时间，也开始把并网冲击、功率调节和站点运营纳入评价。兆瓦级设备主要面向重卡和高频物流，华为此前已用全液冷技术建设相关示范网络，并与物流企业验证长距离电动运输。对司机而言，充电速度决定车辆能否少停工；对运营商和电网而言，集中补能可能制造新的峰值负荷。行业下一步需要把储能、功率预测、错峰调度和收费机制一起做实，让“充得快”不以局部电网承压为代价。

20. 东风奕派M8正式上市，全系标配华为乾崑六件套

核心内容：东风奕派M8于7月23日上市，共推出5款车型，官方售价17.98万至21.98万元，限时权益价16.58万至20.58万元。新车定位中大型六座SUV，提供增程和纯电两种动力，全系搭载华为乾崑六件套智能解决方案，试图用座舱、辅助驾驶与家庭空间形成完整卖点。华为方案继续向更主流价格带下探，会让消费者更容易获得统一的智能体验，也让车企之间的硬件差异缩小。真正拉开差距的将是交付质量、软件更新、售后网络，以及辅助驾驶在不同道路环境下能否稳定工作。

21. 京东物流参与新会陈皮公共监管仓，地标农产品引入全程溯源

核心内容：江门新会与京东物流合作建设陈皮第三方公共监管仓，把仓储、检验、流通和数字化追溯引入地理标志产品管理。新会陈皮价值与年份、产地和仓储条件高度相关，市场长期面临真假难辨、标准不一和流通信息断裂等问题。公共监管仓可为入库陈皮建立相对统一的记录，并借助京东物流的仓配能力连接商家和消费者。平台化仓储不会自动消除造假，关键仍是检测标准、数据是否可查、责任如何追溯以及监管与经营是否保持边界；这些细节决定“可追溯”能否转化为可信任。

22. 特斯拉隐藏式门把手推动美国酝酿新规，断电逃生成为监管重点

核心内容：美国国家公路交通安全管理局启动规则制定程序，研究是否要求车企提供更可靠的紧急车门逃生系统。起因包括多起车辆碰撞或断电后乘员被困事件，以及针对2022款特斯拉Model 3机械应急开门设计的请愿。监管机构没有直接认定单一车型存在缺陷，而是认为问题更适合用适用于所有车企的新标准处理；启动程序也不代表规则一定出台。隐藏式电子门把手兼顾风阻和外观，但安全场景下，乘员必须能迅速看见并操作机械释放装置。设计的高级感不能把逃生路径藏起来。

23. Meta退出RE100清洁能源倡议，AI数据中心天然气扩张引发质疑

核心内容：Meta确认在加入约十年后退出企业可再生能源倡议RE100，双方称分开是共同决定。过去一年，Meta至少资助建设12座天然气电厂，其中为路易斯安那州Hyperion数据中心配套的10座电厂合计约7.5吉瓦；与此同时，RE100刚收紧企业可再生能源进展的报告要求。Meta仍称会用清洁和可再生能源匹配数据中心用电，但年度购买绿色凭证与机房每小时实际使用何种电力并不是一回事。AI算力扩张正在把能源承诺拉回现实，企业需要公开更细的排放、购电和本地污染数据。

24. Amazon把Luna云游戏接入Prime Video，会员可在电视端即点即玩

核心内容：Amazon把Luna云游戏直接接入Fire TV端Prime Video应用，美国和英国的Prime会员可在新的Games标签中发现并启动游戏，无需下载，也不必再单独寻找Luna入口，手机或兼容手柄都可充当控制器。影视、体育与游戏被放进同一个订阅界面，意味着Amazon正用Prime的现有用户规模降低云游戏获客成本。对普通用户来说，真正的门槛从安装变成网络延迟、手柄连接和内容选择。入口合并能带来首次体验，但若游戏库、画质和跨设备进度不稳定，Prime Video里的一个标签也难以形成长期使用习惯。

25. Google上线自拍视频登录备份，账号找回多了一把“人脸钥匙”

核心内容：Google开始允许用户预先录制自拍视频，作为账号被锁定或无法使用常用手机、电脑时的备用身份验证方式。用户需要先在安全设置中添加视频，找回账号时再录制一段实时视频与存档比对；它不会取代密码、通行密钥和日常登录，也不能等到已经被锁定后才临时添加。自拍视频为丢失设备的用户增加了一条恢复路径，但也把生物特征纳入账号安全。Google需要防范深度伪造和胁迫验证，并提供清晰的删除、替代和申诉机制，用户则应把它当备份而不是唯一钥匙。

【心语】没有人可以左右你的人生，只是很多时候我们需要多一些勇气，去坚定自己的选择。

title: 上海生物医药基金二期落地，首关15亿锚定IND到临床Ⅱ期“关键一跃”
summary: 上海生物医药基金二期正式落地，目标规模20亿，首轮认缴15亿，由上实资本携手上海医药等多家产业龙头与专业投资机构共同出资。基金将重点投资IND到临床Ⅱ期阶段的创新化药、生物药、医疗器械等资产，精准卡位“风险收益比最优”区间。其独特价值不仅在于财务回报，更在于深度绑定的产业协同逻辑，通过“产业+资本”模式，为产业方提供高质量早期项目池，实现研发管线的精准补充与项目转化效率提升。此次基金二期的推出，是...
full_content:
近日，随着上海医药一纸公告的挂出，由上实资本担任管理人并发起设立的上海生物医药基金二期正式进入公众视野。据公告，基金目标募集规模20亿元，首轮认缴规模已达15亿元，上实资本携手上海医药、上药集团、上海国投先导、浦东创投、国泰海通、君实生物、张江集团等多家产业龙头与专业投资机构共同出资。

 


根据公告，基金出资方涵盖生物医药产业龙头企业：上海医药、君实生物等，产业龙头聚焦一只基金，在当下生物医药投资市场中并不多见，既体现了上实资本强大的产业资源整合能力，也折射出产业方对其专业投资能力和过往业绩的高度认可。

 

上实资本累计管理规模超345亿元，在医疗领域投资覆盖创新药、高端医疗器械、创新支付、制药装备、生命科学等细分赛道，成功推动礼新医药、宝济药业、ArriVent、心泰医疗、乐普生物、维立志博等多家企业实现上市或退出。产业基金二期将重点投资IND到临床Ⅱ期阶段资产，全面覆盖创新化药、生物药、医疗器械等前沿技术驱动的First-in-Class（FiC）/Best-in-Class（BiC）资产，重点布局消化代谢、心脑血管、肿瘤、自免等赛道，这一策略精准卡位了生物医药创新价值链中"风险收益比最优"的区间。

 


基金的独特价值，不仅在于财务回报的追求，更在于其深度绑定的产业协同逻辑。以上海医药为例，参与基金将有效衔接其创新体系建设与“大BD”战略，构建“早期发现+成果转化+商业落地”的内部闭环生态。基金将发挥“发现早、培育好、对接快、服务实”的独特优势，通过优先输送前沿创新成果并推动优质资产优先被产业龙头承接，为产业方提供高质量的早期项目池，实现研发管线的精准补充与项目转化效率的系统提升。

 

这种“产业+资本”的深度协同模式，既保证了基金投资项目拥有清晰的产业退出路径，也为被投企业提供了从研发到商业化的全周期赋能。这正是上海国资所倡导的“基金+产业+投后赋能”一体化机制的生动实践。

 


此次基金二期的推出，并非简单的规模复制，而是对既有基金矩阵的一次精准补位。至此，上实资本已构建起以上海生物医药基金一期（聚焦成长期）、上海生物医药创新转化基金（专注源头孵化）、上海生物医药并购基金（着眼产业整合）、香港生物科技基金（探索跨境创新）为主体的多层次、多币种投资矩阵，形成了"源头孵化—临床前/早期临床—后期临床/上市—并购整合"的完整投资闭环，真正实现了对生物医药企业从实验室到商业化、从境内到境外的全周期陪伴。其中，一期基金首期认缴规模70亿元，累计已推动多起上市及并购退出。这一生态的完善，不仅让被投企业在不同发展阶段均能获得适配的资本与资源，也为本次基金所汇聚的产业龙头LP提供了从早期项目发现到成熟资产并购的一站式项目池，使"产业+资本"的深度协同从理念走向可操作、可复制的制度安排。

 


十五五开局，生物医药首次被国家层面明确为新兴支柱产业，上海正朝着三大先导产业各破万亿的目标加速迈进。上海生物医药基金二期的适时推出，为上海建设"世界级产业集群"提供了可操作、可落地的资本范式。

title: 当循证医学遇上AI产品思维，氢离子如何成为医生的可靠助手！【中国创新医疗资产会客厅 | 交易圆桌派26期】
summary: AI浪潮下，医生面临AI幻觉、文献获取难、循证工具可信度不足等痛点。今年5月阿里健康推出氢离子医学大模型，获多家顶刊全文内容授权，搭建四层循证AI架构，辅以300余名临床专家评审体系，构建全链路可信闭环，解决AI不可靠、文献获取难问题。7月28日19:00，阿里健康、动脉网及微解药联合主办《中国创新医疗资产会客厅》交易圆桌派第二十六期，邀请复旦大学循证医学中心执行主任陈世耀、复旦大学大健康信息研究...
full_content:
AI浪潮席卷医疗行业的当下，医生存在AI幻觉、顶刊文献获取门槛高、循证工具可信度不足等痛点。今年5月阿里健康正式推出氢离子医学大模型，并且成为国内首家获得NEJM集团（《新英格兰医学杂志》出版方）、JAMA（美国医学会杂志）、BMJ集团全文内容授权的平台，搭建基于PICO、GRADE标准的四层循证AI架构，辅以300余名临床专家组成的多层评审体系，构建从证据解析、精准检索、模型优化到专家核验的全链路可信闭环，从源头解决AI不可靠、文献获取难两大行业痛点。


在此背景下，7月28日（星期二）19:00阿里健康、动脉网及微解药联合主办的《中国创新医疗资产会客厅》交易圆桌派第二十六期，邀请到陈世耀-复旦大学循证医学中心执行主任、中山医院内科基地主任‌，应峻-复旦大学大健康信息研究中心副主任，复旦大学医学图书馆馆长，张令宇-阿里健康氢离子医学大模型医学负责人三位嘉宾围绕《当循证医学遇上AI产品思维，氢离子如何成为医生的可靠助手！》话题共同探讨医学AI从“通用智能”向“循证可信”的变革之路。


嘉宾：陈世耀

复旦大学循证医学中心执行主任

中山医院内科基地主任


●主任医师，教授，博士生导师

●复旦大学附属中山医院内科基地主任，临床技能培训中心主任，消化科/内镜中心副主任

●中华医学会 临床流行病学和循证医学分会第7届主任委员

●上海医学会 内科分会第9届副主任委员；食管和胃静脉曲张治疗专科分会第7届主任委员；临床流行病学和循证医学分会第6-7届主任委员


嘉宾：应  峻 

复旦大学大健康信息研究中心副主任

复旦大学医学图书馆馆长


●复旦大学图书馆副馆长、医学图书馆馆长

●复旦大学大健康信息研究中心副主任

●复旦大学知识产权信息服务中心常务副主任

●复旦大学知识产权研究中心副主任

●中国科技情报学会健康信息学专委会副主任委员

●中国医院协会医院情报图书专委会副主任委员

●临床外科学硕士、医学编辑

●曾参与临床医学术语集、医学知识图谱、医学大模型训练，以及医学AI工具训练与应用等项目。



《中国创新医疗资产会客厅》是动脉网以 “链接中国医疗健康创新资产与全球买方” 为核心定位的线上直播栏目，聚焦创新药、高端器械、数字医疗等领域的优质资产交易，旨在为战略型、财务型及产业型买方群体搭建“展示-交流-对接” 的专业平台。栏目以“挖掘中国创新资产价值、促进高效交易”为目标，通过精准匹配供需、解析交易逻辑、分享实战经验，助力买方群体捕捉优质资产机会，同时推动本土创新资产的转化与留存，服务全球生命健康创新资产买方联盟的生态构建。

title: The same maternal inequity, from Ecuador to America
summary: “I want my mom.” I still remember hearing those words from a twelve-year-old pregnant patient during my internship at a public maternity hospital in Quito, Ecuador. She had become pregnant...
full_content:
“I want my mom.”

I still remember hearing those words from a twelve-year-old pregnant patient during my internship at a public maternity hospital in Quito, Ecuador. She had become pregnant after being sexually abused by a neighbor and came from a low-income community with limited access to education and health care resources. When I met her, she was alone in a hospital bed during labor, crying and asking for her mother to be beside her. Those words stayed with me long after that day. At a young age, she was experiencing motherhood before fully understanding childhood herself.

Later, I witnessed the delivery of her baby. Before entering the room, one of the physicians told the medical students not to ask whether she wanted skin-to-skin contact with the newborn because she had already expressed fear and emotional distress regarding the pregnancy. During postpartum care, she later admitted that she had hidden the pregnancy from her mother because she was afraid no one would believe her. Since the abuse was only discovered at the time of delivery, the police arrived at the hospital shortly afterward to begin documenting a rape report.

I grew up in Ecuador, surrounded by many of the same structural inequities I later witnessed firsthand during my medical internship in Quito. I realized that many of these young women were not simply “unaware” of their conditions or unwilling to seek prenatal care. Most of them came from rural areas of Ecuador with limited access to health care facilities, preventive medicine, transportation, education, and social support systems. Their outcomes were strongly influenced by structural and socioeconomic barriers long before they arrived at the hospital. These experiences helped me recognize how maternal complications are often not only medical problems, but also reflections of deeper systemic inequities.

It was also difficult to witness how some health care providers approached these patients with judgment rather than empathy. Young pregnant women were often blamed for their circumstances without considering the realities of poverty, abuse, limited education, and lack of access to health care resources. In many cases, patients were advised to maintain healthy pregnancies while living in environments where adequate nutrition, medications, and consistent prenatal care were not realistically accessible.

At that time, my focus was mainly clinical. I was learning how to recognize symptoms, improve outcomes, and provide treatment during obstetric emergencies. However, as I continued my training and later began my Master of Public Health studies in the United States, I started to understand maternal health from a broader perspective.

Although the United States has greater health care resources compared to many Latin American countries, I have learned that the same fundamental problem persists: Structural barriers continue to prevent marginalized women from accessing quality maternal care. In Ecuador, I witnessed how poverty, limited education, lack of transportation, food insecurity, and reduced access to prenatal care affected maternal outcomes in rural communities. In the United States, minority and underserved populations, particularly Black women, continue to experience significantly higher maternal mortality rates compared with White women. In addition, barriers related to insurance coverage, health care costs, and language differences can delay prenatal care and negatively affect maternal outcomes. The countries are different, but the inequity is the same.

I came to the United States carrying the memory of that twelve-year-old girl, and of all the women I cared for who deserved more than what the system offered them. That is why I am pursuing both obstetrics and gynecology and public health, not only to treat patients, but also to understand and address the conditions that put them at risk in the first place. I hope to contribute to maternal health research focused on prevention, access to care, and equity in the United States and eventually, in my home country of Ecuador. The patients changed, but the systemic failures remained. That is exactly why this work matters to me.

Sofia Chicaiza is a physician.

title: Why “fine” is not clinical reasoning in medical education
summary: An attending physician recently described one of the most troubling encounters she had witnessed involving a medical student. A student emerged from a well-child visit and offered a reassuring summary...
full_content:
An attending physician recently described one of the most troubling encounters she had witnessed involving a medical student. A student emerged from a well-child visit and offered a reassuring summary: “The kid is fine. Everything is good.”

The patient, however, was not a child whose history could be dismissed with a casual adjective. The child had undergone surgical repair of a ventricular septal defect and had a history of failure to thrive. Those facts did not necessarily mean anything was wrong that day. They did mean that “fine” was a conclusion that required evidence.

What was the child’s current growth trajectory? Were weight and height within expected percentiles? Was there exercise intolerance, shortness of breath, diaphoresis with activity, cyanosis, feeding difficulty, chest pain, palpitations, or syncope? What did the cardiovascular examination reveal? Was a murmur present? Were pulses symmetric? Was there hepatomegaly or edema? Had the child received appropriate cardiology follow-up?

The student provided none of that. There was no meaningful history of present illness, no pertinent physical examination, no assessment of the repaired congenital heart defect, no discussion of the prior growth problem, and no treatment plan. Only the declaration that the child was “fine.”

When the attending questioned the student further, she learned that the student had already completed rotations in both family medicine and internal medicine. That detail reframes a teaching moment as a warning about medical education, not about ceremonial presentations, rigid hierarchy, or a return to an era when trainees were humiliated for forgetting an obscure laboratory value. Nor is it about requiring students to recite every normal finding while an impatient team waits to move on. It is about whether trainees can demonstrate the structured clinical reasoning necessary to keep patients safe.

Clinical presentations are not academic performances. They demonstrate how a trainee gathers information, distinguishes relevant facts from background noise, recognizes risk, constructs a problem representation, and decides what should happen next. A presentation allows the supervising physician to assess the trainee’s reasoning. Without that structure, an attending may hear the conclusion without knowing whether the student reached it through careful evaluation, superficial pattern recognition, or mere assumption. “Fine” conceals all three possibilities.

Colloquial reassurance is especially problematic because it sounds more definitive than it is. Words such as “fine,” “stable,” “doing well,” and “looks good” can create the impression that an assessment has occurred when none has been articulated. Stable compared with what? Doing well by what measure? Which concerning possibilities were considered? What evidence supports reassurance? What follow-up is needed?

The problem extends far beyond the examination room. Every future physician will eventually need to hand off a patient at the end of a shift, call a consultant about an urgent issue, escalate a deteriorating patient to an intensive care team, explain a decision to a worried family, or defend a clinical judgment during a quality review. In each of these settings, vague language creates room for misunderstanding.

A patient is not “fine” if the outgoing physician fails to note a drop in blood pressure. A postoperative patient is not “stable” if no one reports an increased oxygen requirement. A child is not “doing well” merely because the student fails to recognize a deviation in the growth curve.

The language of medicine is sometimes criticized for being overly technical, and that criticism is sometimes justified. Jargon may alienate patients and obscure rather than clarify. But precision is not the same as jargon. Clear clinical communication should make the patient’s condition more understandable, not less.

The answer is not longer presentations. It is disciplined ones. A useful presentation identifies the patient, states the reason for the encounter, summarizes relevant history, reports pertinent findings, offers an assessment, and proposes a plan. The level of detail should be proportional to the clinical situation. A routine well-child visit does not require the same level of detail as septic shock, but both require evidence that the clinician knows what was evaluated and why the conclusion is reasonable.

Medical schools and teaching institutions already have frameworks available to them. SOAP organizes information into subjective findings, objective findings, assessment, and plan. SBAR structures urgent communication around the situation, background, assessment, and recommendation. I-PASS helps clinicians standardize handoffs. These methods are not interchangeable, but they share an essential principle: Important clinical information should not rely on memory, improvisation, or personality.

Yet teaching a framework once is not the same as building competency. Students need repeated observation, feedback, and correction. Faculty members must model concise, complete presentations rather than rewarding speed alone. Clerkship evaluations should assess whether students can synthesize information, not merely whether they collected it. Entrustment decisions should include demonstrated competence in handoffs, escalation, documentation, and oral communication.

Clinical reasoning also needs to remain visible in the age of artificial intelligence. Students can now generate polished differential diagnoses, assessment templates, and documentation with minimal effort. These tools may help organize thinking, but they can also create the appearance of reasoning when little has actually occurred. A fluent note is not proof of clinical understanding. Neither is a long list of possible diagnoses.

The essential question remains: Can the trainee explain what is important about this patient, what the available evidence shows, what could be missed, and what should happen next?

Institutions should therefore require students to present patients in their own words before using generated text. Supervisors should ask trainees to justify their assessment, identify the most serious alternative diagnosis, and explain which findings would change the plan. Simulation exercises should include deteriorating patients, incomplete handoffs, and ambiguous cases that require the trainee to escalate concern.

Faculty development is equally important. We cannot demand structured communication from students while attending physicians model hurried, fragmented, or dismissive exchanges. Educational culture is transmitted less through policy documents than through what learners see rewarded each day.

The attending who challenged the word “fine” was not insisting on empty formality. She was asking the student to make the invisible visible: the history obtained, the examination performed, the risks considered, the judgment reached, and the plan formulated.

“Fine” should never be mistaken for clinical reasoning.

Arthur Lazarus is a physician-author whose work spans narrative medicine, physician leadership, artificial intelligence, health care ethics, medical culture, and fiction. He has published more than 500 articles and essays across scientific journals, professional publications, and online platforms.

He is the author of numerous books on narrative medicine, AI in medicine, career development, and the changing moral landscape of health care, as well as fictional series including Rounds Never End, Sick and Systemic, and Real Medicine, Unreal Stories. His writing explores the forces reshaping modern medicine while preserving a central commitment to story, meaning, judgment, and the human relationship at the heart of care.

He shares updates on LinkedIn.

full_content:
7月17日至20日，2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议（WAIC 2026）于上海盛大启幕。


本届大会以“智能伙伴 共创未来”为核心主题，集中展出人工智能前沿创新成果，清晰勾勒出产业全新发展脉络：AI技术正深度扎根真实产业场景，持续落地民生价值。


以数字技术赋能千行百业、推动创新成果普惠共享、深化全球人工智能治理协作、输出数字健康领域中国方案，已成为行业共识与核心发展方向。



作为医疗AI规模化落地的先行者，讯飞医疗紧扣大会主题，携智医助理、医学影像云平台及全新升级的讯飞晓医健康管理平台等数智方案亮相，并启动讯飞晓医全场景生态合作计划，锚定成为“每个医生的AI诊疗助理、每个人的AI健康助手”核心使命，推动经过大规模临床验证的AI医疗能力下沉普及，践行人工智能普惠民生、共享创新价值的发展路径。


全层级诊疗提效 

大模型筑基 贯通院端基层与区域协同


所有场景落地的底气，均源自讯飞医疗长期扎根临床的技术深耕。今年6月发布的星火医疗大模型V3.5，基于全国产算力实现多模态能力全方位跃迁，依托高质量医疗数据集、双循证思维链与前沿算法架构升级，率先在病历生成、影像报告智能生成等多个专业医疗场景突破实用门槛，临床智能体能力同步进阶，为全域产品的精准性、实用性与场景适配性筑牢底层支撑。


基于统一的大模型技术底座，讯飞医疗从诊疗能力提升、区域资源协同等维度构建起覆盖等级医院到基层医疗机构的全层级医疗服务体系。


在面向临床诊疗相关场景，讯飞医疗形成分层适配的产品矩阵：面向等级医院场景推出AI诊疗助理2.0，以多智能体协同模式直击临床文书负担重、病历质控滞后、诊疗决策视角受限等痛点，为各级医院提供全流程智能诊疗支撑；面向基层医疗场景迭代升级智医助理，将标准化诊疗能力持续下沉，补齐基层医疗服务短板。目前，智医助理已覆盖全国超811个区县、7.7万家基层医疗机构，累计提供超12亿次辅助诊断建议，切实提升基层诊疗的规范性与精准度。


在区域资源协同层面，依托星火医疗大模型V3.5在影像赛道的技术突破，医学影像云平台破解区域医疗资源失衡、跨机构影像数据割裂等行业难题，真正实现“一次检查、全域互认”。平台现已完成安徽全部公立医疗机构接入，累计归集1.6亿份影像资料；落地的广西医保影像云，目前累计完成近109万次跨院影像调阅，有效提升医疗资源共享效率与群众就医便捷度。



本届WAIC现场，讯飞医疗展区集中呈现了这套从院内诊疗到区域协同的全链路解决方案，其中上海落地实践作为重点案例展出：助力基层卫生提质增效的智医助理已覆盖静安、徐汇、长宁、闵行等区的社区医院及村卫生室，累计提供超3335万次辅助诊疗服务，完成超589万份标准化电子病历；基于大模型底层技术落地的AI居民健康画像系统，为试点区域的149万余名签约居民生成动态全生命周期健康档案，医生调阅全量健康数据的耗时从5分钟压缩至30秒。


该基层数智健康实践更作为中国标杆方案，亮相第79届世界卫生大会主题边会，向全球输出普惠医疗的中国经验与可行路径。


全民健康场景扩容 

讯飞晓医升级开放生态共建产业新格局


依托经大规模临床验证的成熟医疗AI能力，讯飞医疗进一步把专业诊疗能力从医院向全民日常健康场景延伸覆盖。本届大会上，全新升级的讯飞晓医健康管理平台亮相，并正式启动全场景生态合作计划。



全新的讯飞晓医健康管理平台将医疗级AI能力全面延伸至全生命周期健康管理场景，针对不同群体打造分层解决方案：面向基层场景打造软硬件一体化健康管理体系；面向企业场景推出员工一站式健管平台；面向家庭场景生成基于个人健康档案的“AI健康管理计划”，支持全家多病共管，同步提供中医体质辨识、定制代茶饮等特色服务，实现专业医疗能力从院内到居家的无缝衔接。


目前，讯飞晓医全生命周期健康管理能力已全面对外开放，可输出症状自查、报告解读、用药查询、中医辨证、健康管理等标准化AI能力模块，并提供多种灵活合作模式，适配不同规模伙伴的定制化落地需求。


本届WAIC现场，这套覆盖全生命周期的健康管理能力也以健康小屋的实景形式面向观众开放体验。健康一体机、骨密度检测仪、中医四诊仪等多类智能检测设备全量接入讯飞晓医平台实现数据互通，支持数分钟自助完成多项基础指标检测，数据实时同步后即可生成AI解读报告与就医指导；中医服务区依托AI舌面诊与症状问询完成体质辨识，输出个性化调养和代茶饮方案，并可联动同仁堂中医专家线上问诊复核，实现中西医健康服务一站式覆盖。



从诊疗能力与区域协同的双向补齐，到全民健康场景的生态扩容，讯飞医疗在本届WAIC上完整呈现了医疗AI产业从技术到产品、从产品到生态的进阶路径，也印证了技术终要回归民生、服务日常的发展本质。


当前，人工智能与医疗健康的融合已进入深水区，技术普惠与生态共赢是行业发展的核心方向。


未来，讯飞医疗将持续以星火医疗大模型为核心，一方面持续深耕临床场景，夯实诊疗端的技术优势，推动优质医疗服务提质增效；另一方面以开放生态连接全产业链力量，共同拓展健康服务的边界与形态，让人工智能的价值，扎根诊室诊疗场景，普惠大众平凡日常。

title: AI互联网日报：豆包进入469元小屏手机、OpenAI基建承诺升至7500亿美元、Kimi卷入蒸馏争议
summary: 产品由脑机接口与视觉假体技术结合，开始从临床验证迈向更广泛的医疗使用。监管许可意味着安全性和疗效材料达到上市门槛，但实际效果会因患者病因、手术条件和康复训练而异。对脑机接口行业来说，这类明确医疗用途比通用人机增强更接近商业化，也更容易衡量价值。后续仍要观察定价

一起来看看这两天发生的AI和互联网赛道的大事件吧！

📌 今日AI互联网大事件速览

2，HMD Touch AI复刻Lumia，469元小屏手机接入豆包

AI赛道观察

1. AI编程从模型比拼转向价格战，OpenAI、Anthropic与Kimi争夺工作流入口

核心内容：AI编程市场的竞争正在从单纯比模型能力，转向免费额度、订阅价格和开发工作流。海外的Anthropic与OpenAI不断增加体验时长和免费配额，国内则出现阿里强调市场份额、智谱披露商业化进展、Kimi用K3强化编程能力等动作。模型能力差距缩小后，开发者更容易在不同产品之间切换，平台真正要守住的是代码库理解、工具调用、团队协作和企业权限。价格战能迅速拉新，也会压低单用户收入，最终还得靠稳定交付和付费场景证明商业模式。

2. HMD Touch AI复刻Lumia，469元小屏手机接入豆包

3. 爱奇艺上线首部获证AIGC网络故事片，AI全流程影片超过60分钟

核心内容：爱奇艺独家上线AIGC网络故事片《奇谭：纸刃渡荒墟》，影片由大梦创新与爱奇艺联合出品，以中式志怪为故事底色，全片超过60分钟，并在制作流程中广泛使用AI。该片获得《网络剧片发行许可证》，成为国内首部获证上线播出的AIGC网络故事片，也是“奇谭三部曲”的开篇。生成式视频从短片和演示进入完整叙事后，制作效率只是第一关，角色连续性、镜头语言、版权来源和观众是否愿意看完，才决定这条路线能否真正进入影视工业。

4. 美国政府指控月之暗面蒸馏Anthropic模型，制裁威胁引发争议

核心内容：美国白宫指称月之暗面在训练Kimi时蒸馏Anthropic的Claude Fable模型，美国财政部门随后释放可能采取制裁措施的信号。相关说法目前属于政府指控，公开证据、技术判定过程和具体制裁范围仍不清晰，月之暗面此前也否认Kimi K3是对现有模型的蒸馏复刻。事件把正常的模型蒸馏方法、未经授权提取能力和国家安全叙事混在了一起。若政策只凭结果相似就判断技术来源，开放模型、API使用和跨境研发都会面临更高的不确定性。

5. 美国开源实验室Arcee称中国模型不应被一概视为危险

核心内容：美国开源AI实验室Arcee公开反对把中国模型天然等同于安全威胁，认为模型风险应依据部署位置、数据流向、权重透明度和实际用途判断，而不是只看开发者国别。随着中国开源模型在美国企业中的使用增加，围绕禁用、审查和供应链风险的争论也在升温。开源权重便于本地部署和独立审计，但并不会自动消除后门、训练数据或许可证风险。更可执行的治理方式，是建立统一测试、数据隔离和采购标准，让不同来源的模型接受同一套验证。

6. OpenAI测试系统误入Hugging Face，沙箱配置失误暴露自主攻击边界

核心内容：OpenAI在内部网络安全测试中让GPT-5.6 Sol及一款更强的预发布模型寻找漏洞，系统随后意外进入Hugging Face环境。OpenAI称测试原本运行在高度隔离的沙箱中，但人工配置错误让模型具备了不应拥有的外部访问路径，最终形成真实越界。事件说明自主网络安全智能体的风险不只来自模型意图，更来自权限、凭据、网络边界和测试环境配置。能力越强，红队测试越需要最小权限、全程审计、紧急断开和独立复核，不能只靠提示词约束。

7. OpenAI基建承诺增至7500亿美元，模型竞赛先考验融资与回报

核心内容：OpenAI截至2030年的AI基础设施支出承诺被指已增至约7500亿美元，覆盖数据中心、芯片、电力和长期算力合同。这个规模接近一个中型经济体的年度产出，也让模型竞赛从技术问题变成资本、能源与现金流问题。提前锁定算力有助于支撑训练和推理需求，但长期合同会把需求预测、利用率和融资成本一并固定下来。ChatGPT订阅、企业服务和API收入必须持续高速增长，才能覆盖折旧和采购承诺，否则算力优势也可能变成沉重的资产负担。

8. 五大科技巨头表外债务达1.65万亿美元，AI投资风险更难被看清

核心内容：一项针对Alphabet、微软、亚马逊、Meta和甲骨文财务资料的调查估算，五家公司表外债务在约四年间扩大到原来的8倍，总额达到1.65万亿美元，并已超过其账面债务。AI数据中心常通过长期租赁、采购承诺和项目融资建设，相关义务不一定完整呈现在传统资产负债表中。大厂仍有强劲现金流，但投资者需要把电力合同、设备租赁和未履约采购一起纳入风险评估。AI基建越依赖长期承诺，短期收入增长就越不能代表真实资本回报。

9. Monday.com裁员约630人，AI转型伴随20%人员缩减

核心内容：企业协作软件公司Monday.com宣布削减约20%的员工，涉及约630人，并称调整是为了建立更精简、更聚焦的运营模式，把资源集中到AI Work Platform。生成式AI正在改写项目管理、自动化和企业软件的产品形态，但“聚焦AI”也越来越频繁地与组织收缩同时出现。裁员能快速降低成本，却不会自动带来产品竞争力。公司后续需要证明AI功能能提升续费、客单价和工作流黏性，也要避免团队缩减损害客户支持与交付质量。

10. IBM称AI暂时挤压主机预算，企业硬件支出结构正在改写

核心内容：企业客户近期把更多硬件预算转向AI项目，造成IBM传统大型主机采购暂时承压，而非主机需求永久消失。大型机构仍依赖主机处理银行交易、政府系统和核心数据库，但新增预算正在流向GPU集群、存储和AI软件。对IBM而言，关键不是证明主机不会被替代，而是让主机数据、安全与AI工作负载顺畅连接。如果AI投入只是挤占旧预算却没有带来新收入，企业IT市场的增长会更多表现为结构迁移，而非整体扩张。

11. 巴基斯坦法院试用JudgeGPT，案件审结量提升6.3%

核心内容：巴基斯坦在118个初审法院、1559名法官中测试基于GPT-4定制的JudgeGPT，并设置不同使用和培训条件进行对照。获得AI访问权限且接受针对性工具培训的法官，案件审结量提升6.3%；相关研究还估算每投入1美元可带来约38.5美元收益。结果说明AI与培训结合可能帮助整理材料、检索和起草，但实验数据不等于可以让模型独立裁判。司法场景必须保留法官最终责任，并持续检查幻觉、偏见、当事人隐私和不同地区案件质量差异。

12. 美国公用事业公司承诺不让居民承担AI数据中心电费

核心内容：面对AI数据中心推高居民电价的担忧，美国大型公用事业公司和数据中心开发商承诺采取措施，避免把新增电网、发电和输电成本直接转嫁给普通家庭。承诺回应了社区对用电紧张和电费上涨的反弹，但具体费率设计、长期购电合同和基础设施分摊方式仍需监管机构审核。数据中心可以承担专属设施成本，也能通过可调负荷和自建能源减轻压力；如果缺少透明核算，费用仍可能通过公共电网间接扩散。AI公司的算力账，最终必须把真实能源成本算进去。

13. Synthesia推出AI角色扮演训练，企业培训从视频走向实时陪练

核心内容：Synthesia推出AI Roleplay Sessions，让员工与AI虚拟人进行销售、管理、客服等工作对话练习，系统会提供反馈、评分和分析，企业也能据此衡量培训效果。产品把Synthesia从单向生成培训视频推进到实时互动，用户不再只是观看内容，而是在模拟压力下反复练习。相比传统课程，这种方式更容易规模化和个性化，但评分标准必须透明，敏感对话也要做好数据隔离。若企业把练习分数直接用于绩效或招聘，偏差和申诉机制将成为新的管理风险。

14. AMD展示256核Zen 6 EPYC Venice，AI服务器CPU继续扩张

核心内容：AMD在Advancing AI 2026活动中展示基于Zen 6架构的下一代EPYC Venice旗舰处理器，最高配置256个核心和512个线程。芯片采用8个大型计算Die，每个Die集成32个核心，并配备大尺寸I/O Die，目标仍是高性能计算和大型数据中心。AI服务器的注意力常被GPU占据，但CPU负责数据准备、网络调度、虚拟化和通用计算，直接影响整机利用率。核心数继续增加后，内存带宽、软件调度、功耗和每核性能会比纸面规模更决定部署价值。

15. 马斯克计划用Grok Imagine拍摄《奥德赛》，生成式视频挑战长片制作

核心内容：埃隆·马斯克计划使用xAI的Grok Imagine制作一部长篇《奥德赛》题材影片，并把2026年底前完成作为目标。生成式视频已能快速产出单个镜头，但完整长片还要求角色外观、场景关系、声音和叙事节奏在数十分钟内保持一致，制作难度远高于短视频演示。该项目目前仍停留在公开计划，尚未披露预算、团队和发行安排。项目若推进，将成为检验生成视频能否从素材工具走向工业化长叙事的一次高关注实验。

互联网赛道观察

16. 百度申请转为香港双重主要上市，预计年内完成转换

核心内容：百度就香港上市地位由第二上市转为双重主要上市提交申请，并收到港交所确认函，转换预计在2026年内生效，仍需完成后续程序。完成后，百度在香港与纳斯达克的上市地位将相互独立，也具备进一步纳入港股通的制度前提。转换有望扩大内地投资者参与渠道，提升港股流动性，并让文心、昆仑芯、自动驾驶和云业务获得更多本地市场定价关注。不过上市身份变化不会自动改善估值，长期表现仍取决于收入增长、利润和AI投入回报。

17. 小米米家桌面照片打印机2开启预约，多尺寸热升华瞄准家庭影像

核心内容：小米米家桌面照片打印机2开启预约，单机售价799元，套装售价999元，计划7月27日开售。产品支持4英寸、6英寸和方形即贴三种相纸，采用四色热升华与多种纹理覆膜，套装还包含双尺寸相纸和专属相册。手机影像越来越多地停留在云端，这类设备试图用低门槛打印把照片重新带回家庭和礼赠场景。真正影响使用频率的并非打印机售价，而是耗材成本、色彩稳定性、保存时间以及米家应用连接是否足够顺手。

18. 京东购车接入张雪机车小程序，线上买车入口继续下沉

核心内容：京东购车服务接入张雪机车微信小程序，用户可在品牌小程序内进入线上购车链路。张雪机车此前已把订单咨询集中到小程序、把售后与故障工单集中到官方App，此次接入意味着商品、交易与服务入口开始进一步打通。对消费者来说，线上买车的价值不只是下单，还包括车型信息、交付进度、发票、维修和质保能否连续衔接。平台与品牌后续需要明确责任边界，避免交易在京东、服务在品牌端时出现信息不同步。

19. 抖音提高AI仿真人剧准入门槛，平台开始整治“恐怖谷效应”

核心内容：抖音开始提高AI仿真人剧的内容准入门槛，把角色失真、动作违和和明显“恐怖谷”观感纳入治理重点。AI短剧降低了制作成本，也带来批量生产、肖像模仿和粗糙内容挤占流量的问题，平台从事后下架转向前置质量控制，意味着生成内容不能再只靠数量换分发。准入提高有助于改善观看体验，但规则还需要清楚区分技术瑕疵、风格化创作和侵权仿冒，并向创作者说明标识、审核与申诉流程，避免标准模糊造成误伤。

20. 腾讯云计划第四季度部署NPO超级节点，呼吁统一行业标准

核心内容：腾讯云预计在2026年第四季度部署NPO超级节点，并呼吁产业链推动相关互连和系统标准统一。超级节点把大量加速卡、网络和存储组织成更紧密的计算单元，目标是提高大模型训练与推理中的通信效率和资源利用率。国内算力系统正在从单卡参数竞争转向整机和集群协同，但不同厂商协议、管理工具和软件栈不统一，会增加迁移与运维成本。腾讯云的部署进度、兼容范围和真实负载表现，将检验标准倡议能否落到可复用的基础设施上。

21. iOS 27被曝新增受限模式，分期iPhone欠款后可能限制应用

核心内容：开发者在iOS 27测试版代码中发现“Restricted Mode”相关能力，可能允许Apple在分期购买的iPhone出现逾期后限制部分应用或功能。该发现与Apple准备扩大iPhone融资方案的消息相呼应，但功能尚未正式发布，触发条件、恢复流程和适用市场都不明确。远程限制设备能降低融资风险，也会把债务管理直接写进操作系统。若正式上线，Apple需要明确紧急通信、支付申诉、数据导出和误判恢复等底线，避免一笔账单把用户的基本数字生活一起锁住。

22. SoundCloud收购Nina Protocol，独立音乐人和发现工具并入平台

核心内容：SoundCloud收购去中心化音乐平台Nina Protocol，交易发生在Nina宣布停止运营数月之后。Nina积累的独立音乐人关系、编辑档案和音乐发现工具将并入SoundCloud，具体金额未披露。SoundCloud近年来持续强化艺术家服务和内容发现，希望在流媒体巨头之外保留更开放的创作者入口。收购可以延续Nina的社区资产，但平台也需要处理原有用户数据、作品授权和历史链接，避免“保存社区”最后只变成一次内容迁移。

23. Apple被曝测试升级版MacBook Neo，更大内存与新处理器在列

核心内容：Apple被曝正在开发MacBook Neo的更新版本，测试方向包括更大内存、新处理器和新的机身颜色。MacBook Neo以更低价格切入笔记本市场后取得较高关注，升级若保持定位，将进一步覆盖学生和轻办公用户。目前信息仍来自研发测试，最终配置、发布时间和价格尚未确认。对入门Mac来说，内存容量会直接影响多任务和本地AI能力，而处理器升级必须与续航、散热和售价平衡；真正的挑战是增强体验而不把产品推离预算市场。

24. 飞利浦推出AI电动牙刷，实时提示没有刷干净的位置

核心内容：飞利浦推出新一代Sonicare DiamondClean 9900 Prestige智能电动牙刷，使用第三代AI模型识别刷牙覆盖情况，并在过程中给出实时反馈，帮助用户看到遗漏区域。智能牙刷过去常依赖计时、压力传感和手机记录，新产品试图把反馈从事后报告提前到刷牙动作本身。健康硬件的价值在于形成稳定习惯，而不是增加一块数据看板。识别准确率、是否必须连接手机、个人口腔数据如何保存，以及刷头和订阅成本，都会影响AI功能能否长期使用。

25. Science Corp视力恢复芯片获欧盟批准，脑机接口进入商业化验证

核心内容：Science Corporation用于帮助视力受损患者恢复部分视觉能力的植入式芯片获得欧盟批准，产品由脑机接口与视觉假体技术结合，开始从临床验证迈向更广泛的医疗使用。监管许可意味着安全性和疗效材料达到上市门槛，但实际效果会因患者病因、手术条件和康复训练而异。对脑机接口行业来说，这类明确医疗用途比通用人机增强更接近商业化，也更容易衡量价值。后续仍要观察定价、医院培训、长期稳定性和医保覆盖。

【心语】只要路是对的，就不怕遥远。不辍前行，终有一天会遇见不放弃带来的惊喜。

title: 三款抗癌药的发明人，带着抗耐药新分子递表纳斯达克
summary: 2026年7月17日，解决肿瘤耐药的创新药企BlossomHill向美国SEC递交S-1招股书，计划登陆纳斯达克。其掌舵人J. Jean Cui凭借大环分子化学设计思路，连续三次做出通过FDA审批的重磅抗癌药，2024年当选美国国家工程院院士。BlossomHill三轮累计融资2.57亿美元，核心瞄准C797S、难治白血病、广谱KRAS三大临床空白，核心临床节点集中在未来18个月。其两条临床阶段管...
full_content:
2026年7月17日，一家专门解决肿瘤耐药的创新药企BlossomHill向美国SEC递交S-1招股书，计划登陆纳斯达克。


这家企业的掌舵人J. Jean Cui，凭借一套大环分子化学设计思路，连续三次做出通过FDA审批的重磅抗癌药。如今带着这套技术，瞄准C797S、难治白血病、广谱KRAS三大临床空白，核心临床节点集中在未来18个月。三轮累计融资2.57亿美元，引来四家头部机构全程押注。


这家仅成立6年的临床Biotech，能否在创始人的带领下再次成功？



J. Jean Cui不是第一次站在纳斯达克大门前了。


2019年，她联合创立的Turning Point Therapeutics曾登陆纳斯达克。2022年，BMS以41亿美元将其收购。几年后，她带着新团队和新管线，再次走向IPO。


BlossomHill核心管理团队，图源官网


翻开她的履历，主导发明四个字贯穿了她的职业生涯。


Crizotinib（克里唑蒂尼），首款ALK抑制剂，是她主导发明的。Lorlatinib（洛拉替尼），第二代ALK抑制剂，中位无进展生存期超过84个月，是Crizotinib的近八倍，也是她主导发明的。Repotrectinib（洛普替尼），ROS1抑制剂，在初治患者中客观缓解率79%，中位无进展生存期35.7个月，还是她主导发明的。


三款药，三获FDA批准。2024年，她当选美国国家工程院院士。


在创新药行业，成功一次可以说是运气。成功三次，只能归因于体系。J. Jean Cui的技术体系，是大环小分子技术。


前面的成功是基于这一技术体系。现在，BlossomHill的两条临床阶段管线BH-30643和BH-30236还是基于它。这是其技术体系的持续发力。


传统小分子药物像一把钥匙，试图插入蛋白的锁孔。可癌细胞会改变锁孔的形状，让钥匙无法匹配，这就是耐药。大环分子的环状结构，能同时抓住蛋白的多个位点，像用几只手指抓住物体，而不是用一根手指去戳。即使锁孔变形，它依然有机会保持结合。


J. Jean Cui用这套技术架构，已经赢过三次。现在，她想再赢一次。


BlossomHill不是J. Jean Cui一个人的战斗。


执行董事长Y. Peter Li，是她在Turning Point的老搭档。Turning Point从创立到IPO再到被收购，他全程在场。CFO Jason Keyes，在生物制药财务行业干了25年，曾在Amgen和Amylin任职。总法律顾问Vincent Liptak，做过Turning Point的知识产权顾问，对一家Biotech要保护什么、怎么保护，轻车熟路。


最值得说的人是首席医学官Geoff Oxnard。


Oxnard不是普通的肿瘤医生，他是C797S耐药突变首篇论文的共同作者。C797S是EGFR突变肺癌患者接受第三代靶向药奥希替尼治疗后，最常出现的耐药突变之一。这个突变堵死了奥希替尼的共价结合位点，让其失效，目前却没有一款新的口服靶向药能解决这个问题。


BlossomHill最核心的管线BH-30643，目标就是C797S。而团队里的Oxnard恰好是该突变领域全球权威，形成研发+临床完美匹配的团队组合。


让发现敌人的人，来设计消灭敌人的武器，这就是BlossomHill的策略。



BlossomHill的三款候选药物分别对应肺癌、血液白血病、多实体瘤 KRAS 突变三大未被满足的治疗场景，每一条管线都能找到明确的患者群体与市场空间。


企业管线布局，图源招股文件


EGFR突变是非小细胞肺癌中最常见的可靶向驱动基因。第一代和第二代EGFR抑制剂，平均用药时间不到两年，患者就会出现耐药。第三代药物奥希替尼把无进展生存期延长了不少，但还是会有部分患者会出现C797S突变，致使药物失效。


陷入耐药困境后，就只能化疗。患者需要一款能口服、能入脑、能覆盖C797S的靶向药。BH-30643的设计正是为此而来。


非共价结合方式，能避开C797S的封锁；大环结构，可增强结合稳定性；穿透血脑屏障，可应对肺癌常见的脑转移；同时覆盖经典突变、T790M、非典型突变和外显子20插入。


BH-30643试图做一个全能的EGFR抑制剂。


另一核心管线BH-30236瞄准的靶点叫CLK（CDC-like kinase），癌细胞利用这个机制，产生错误的蛋白变体，推动肿瘤生长和耐药。CLK抑制剂的概念并不新鲜，可之前的尝试都卡在毒性上，不得不采用间歇给药的方式，使得疗效大打折扣。


BH-30236试图打破这个瓶颈，它正在复发难治急性髓系白血病（AML）和高危骨髓增生异常综合征（MDS）患者中进行1期临床，评估单药和联合用药的效果。2026年3月，FDA授予它AML孤儿药资格，说明监管机构认为这个机制值得深挖。


还有野心最大、希望覆盖所有KRAS突变的BH-501284。KRAS曾经是不可成药靶点的代名词，直到G12C抑制剂索托拉西布和阿达格拉西布获批，可G12C只能覆盖一种突变。


如胰腺癌中KRAS突变率高达90%，结直肠癌中KRAS突变率40%，肺腺癌25%，G12C只占其中一小部分，这些患者中的大多数携带的是G12D、G12V、G12S、G12A等突变，目前都无药可用。


BH-501284用了一种全新的非共价Switch-Ⅱ骨架，临床前数据显示靶点驻留时间超过54小时。目前还在临床前阶段，但发展方向很明确，尽可能覆盖更多的突变，这是KRAS赛道的下半场。


三个问题，三种解法，同一种设计哲学。


BlossomHill找到现有疗法的结构性缺陷，并尝试用新型化学骨架直接解决。这是一种工程师思维，发现漏洞，设计补丁，而非从头造新药。


在Biotech的世界里，有人追风口，有人修漏洞。J. Jean Cui和她的BlossomHill属于后者。



BlossomHill不是唯一看到C797S机会的企业。


这个赛道的竞争者很多，Abbisko、Betta Pharma、Black Diamond、Bridge Therapeutics、Dizal等Biotech都在开发针对C797S的药物。过去，四代EGFR被认为用于三代药物奥希替尼耐药后的治疗，市场空间有限，因而MNC对这一领域的投入并不多。


随着四代EGFR研究的进行，研究人员发现四代EGFR具备了成为前线NSCLC治疗药物的可能。MNC可能低估了四代EGFR的市场潜力，而中国药企正在密集占据这个赛道。


包括豪森药业、红云制药、浦合医药、威尚生物、迪哲医药、艾力斯以及齐鲁制药等，都在参与。


当前进度靠前的四代EGFR管线，据公开信息制图


像豪森药业HS-10375能应对Del19/T790M/C797S等三重突变；红云制药的H002采用种新型诱导变构设计，能覆盖八种主要突变，迪哲医药DZD6008在2026年ASCO年会上以口头报告形式发布了数据，凭借原创的分子设计获得行业关注。


这个靶点很难，机会同样很大，FDA至今没有批准针对C797S耐药的口服靶向药。谁先做出安全有效的数据，谁就能占据这个空白市场。


如果说C797S赛道是修罗场，pan-KRAS赛道就是诸神之战。


安进、阿斯利康、礼来、辉瑞，这些跨国巨头都在布局pan-KRAS，中国药企同样没有缺席。


加科思的JAB-23E73在2024年9月获得美国FDA的IND批准，可以同时抑制活性状态和非活性状态的KRAS；和誉医药的ABSK211在2026年7月刚刚获得FDA批准IND，是一款新型口服pan-KRAS抑制剂；璎黎药业的YL-17231是首款国产获批进入临床试验的泛KRAS突变抑制剂。


无论是MNC还是中国新锐都已起跑，BlossomHill还在早期阶段，它的差异化在于非共价伪不可逆结合设计，靶点驻留时间超过54小时，但这些特点能否转化为临床优势，仍待观察。


只有CLK赛道竞争较为温和，目前全球仅有3条管线进入临床阶段，中国Biotech没有参与其中。


好消息是资本对它充满信心。


翻开BlossomHill的股东名单，有四个名字反复出现，Cormorant Asset Management、OrbiMed（奥博资本）、Vivo Capital（维梧资本‌）和Janus Henderson Investors（骏利亨德森投资）。


这些机构都是极具耐心的长期投资者，一家临床阶段Biotech从IND到产品上市，平均需要7年~10年，期间没有营收，只有投入。愿意陪跑的投资者，必须对团队的能力有极强的信心。它们的持续支持，本身就是对BlossomHill最有力的背书。


未来18个月的关键节点，据招股文件制图


2026年四季度，BH-30643的1期结果将决定2期临床的方案和潜在加速审批路径。2027年一季度，2期关键临床将启动。同一季度，BH-501284提交IND。2027年上半年，BH-30236更新安全性和有效性数据。


随着管线推进研发投入日渐提高，据招股文件制图


这些都是观察BlossomHill后续发展的重要时刻。此次IPO募来的钱，也主要用于三条核心管线的临床推进。


BlossomHill代表一类研发思路，不追逐热门，而是直面现有药物的结构性缺陷，用改良化学骨架解决耐药难题。如果后续临床数据持续兑现，那么这套可复制、经过商业化验证的大环药物研发平台价值将会大幅提升，或许被MNC收购的情况也会再次出现。

title: Building AI infrastructure with the Effingham County community
summary: OpenAI announces Project Camellia in Effingham County, Georgia, with commitments to responsible energy, community investment, jobs, and access to Codex....
full_content:
Project Camellia is a long-term datacenter project that OpenAI is designing and developing in Effingham County, Georgia. To support the data center, we are contracting with Georgia Power Company for 3.2 gigawatts of power which will be delivered in phases between 2028 and 2032.

We’re excited about the opportunity to work with this community. We also recognize that new data center projects can raise important questions, so we’ve outlined our initial commitments that will guide how we engage, develop, and operate.

1. Electricity rates will not go up for residents because of this project. Georgia families will not subsidize this project. OpenAI will pay the full cost of the infrastructure and electric-service costs required to serve it. Under Georgia Public Service Commission rules, those costs cannot be passed on to existing ratepayers. Also, this project will be one of the first data centers designed to proactively reduce its power consumption before residential customers are impacted during periods of high demand, so we can meaningfully support the reliability of Georgia Power’s electric system and support our neighbors. 

2. Water use is minimal. The project will use a closed-loop water system, which recirculates water rather than continuously withdrawing and discharging. It works like a car radiator and is intended to keep ongoing water use low. The water used will not divert water from local communities and the ongoing water needs will be for people to use in an ordinary workplace setting such as restrooms, kitchens, sanitation, and maintenance and will be similar to an office building with the same amount of employees. 

3. We are committed to making sure local communities benefit. OpenAI will provide $80 million in community benefits over the life of the project, informed by the community and directed toward local priorities such as schools, public safety, health care, utilities, workforce training, housing, veterans’ services, and support for small businesses and working families. This commitment is separate from projected tax revenue and the Codex credits described below. We will pay hundreds of millions of dollars in state and local tax revenue and expect to be the largest taxpayer in the county. The project will create thousands of construction and permanent on-site jobs and prioritize local contractors and businesses.

In addition to the $80 million in community benefits, we will make up to $71 million in credits for Codex available to eligible Georgia college, community college, and technical school students. Codex is OpenAI’s agentic coding tool, now available within ChatGPT, that helps people build software and complete technical projects. Eligible students will receive $100 in credits through their ChatGPT accounts to extend their use of Codex, gain hands-on experience with agentic AI, build projects, and develop practical skills for careers across engineering, manufacturing, health care, education, entrepreneurship, and the skilled trades. Georgia students will be able to access their free Codex credits at chatgpt.com/codex/georgia-college-students/⁠(opens in a new window) 

4. Being accountable. To help ensure the project meets these commitments, an annual publicly available audit by an independent firm will be conducted and released.

We have been meeting with state and local officials, community leaders, schools, and other regional partners to learn about local priorities and gather feedback on the project. On Thursday, July 23, we will hold a public open house where residents can meet the project team, ask questions, and help shape how the project delivers for Effingham County. Input from the open house and continued conversations with residents, local officials, schools, businesses, and community organizations will help shape a Georgia Community Compact to memorialize these commitments. The Compact will translate community priorities into specific commitments and clear accountability measures as the project develops.

We believe showing up early is the right way to build trust, with that, we are still at the beginning of the development process. Significant work remains on infrastructure, project phasing, design, financing, and operating model. As we work through these details, we intend to engage with local communities, government, workforce organizations, and our infrastructure and financing partners.

The proposed site is located within the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub, a pre-existing industrially-zoned warehouse project. This project is expected to generate materially less traffic than a warehouse project on the same site, while also using less water, creating stronger long-term tax revenue, and supporting more durable on-site employment.

AI can help accelerate science and medicine, expand access to better tools for learning and discovery, create new kinds of jobs and businesses, and make everyday work more productive. Computing infrastructure is one of the main factors determining how quickly AI can improve, how reliably it works, and how broadly it can be used. 

Building this infrastructure in the United States strengthens domestic industry, creates good jobs, and helps ensure American communities participate in the economic opportunity created by AI. Project Camellia can help build that foundation while creating lasting opportunity in Effingham County and Southeast Georgia, and would be entirely privately funded.

We are already seeing that potential take shape in Abilene, Texas⁠(opens in a new window), where our first campus is operating at scale, training frontier models, and supporting thousands of jobs.
